about_blocks.text: Pacifica Treatment Centre: Non-Profit Residential Addiction Treatment in Vancouver, BC
about_blocks.html: Pacifica Treatment Centre: Non-Profit Residential Addiction Treatment in Vancouver, BC

about_blocks.text: Pacifica Treatment Centre is a non-profit, charitable addiction treatment centre in East Vancouver that has been running since 1977. It offers in-residence primary treatment for adults 19 and older who are dealing with problematic substance use, and it describes its programs as trauma-informed and concurrent-capable, so mental health and trauma are addressed alongside substance use.
about_blocks.html: Pacifica Treatment Centre is a non-profit, charitable addiction treatment centre in East Vancouver that has been running since 1977. It offers in-residence primary treatment for adults 19 and older who are dealing with problematic substance use, and it describes its programs as trauma-informed and concurrent-capable, so mental health and trauma are addressed alongside substance use.

about_blocks.text: The publicly funded program lasts 84 days and is funded primarily through Vancouver Coastal Health. Referrals and the waitlist run through Vancouver Coastal Health's Central Addiction Intake Team (CAIT), and the centre says the wait is usually 8 to 12 weeks. Pacifica also has a privately funded option with stays of 35 to 84 days, but its admissions page lists private-pay stays and self-referral as currently on hiatus.

about_blocks.text: Treatment is part of a longer plan. Pacifica maps out roughly 24 months of contact for each person: pre-engagement while you wait, a first week of orientation, primary treatment, the Integrative Wellness and Resiliency programs, then continuing care and alumni services. During pre-engagement you can come in for the weekly community lunch, tour the building and meet staff before your start date.

about_blocks.text: Days in residence mix group therapy, one-on-one counselling, cognitive behavioural therapy, psychoeducation workshops, mindfulness and yoga. Creative arts therapy, music, acupuncture and Reiki are offered too, along with staff-led walks, runs, hikes and outings. Each person has a private, single-occupancy room, and the kitchen serves three chef-prepared meals and three snacks a day.

about_blocks.text: The building was purpose-built between 1990 and 1993 in a California style, with a large inner meditation courtyard, skylights and gardens, on a quiet residential street a short walk from SkyTrain. Pacifica does not run a detox unit. If an assessment shows you need more withdrawal management than the centre can safely provide, staff refer you to a partner withdrawal management service and arrange your return afterwards.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Pacifica Treatment Centre

faqs.question: Is Pacifica Treatment Centre publicly funded?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Pacifica's 84-day in-residence primary treatment program is publicly funded, mainly through Vancouver Coastal Health, for BC residents aged 19 and over. Government or ministry funded clients may be partly or fully funded up to $45 a day for per diem expenses, and donations subsidise the rest of the cost. A privately funded option exists, but the centre lists it as currently on hiatus.

Government or ministry funded clients may be partly or fully funded up to $45 a day for per diem expenses, and donations subsidise the rest of the cost. A privately funded option exists, but the centre lists it as currently on hiatus.

faqs.question: How do I get a referral to Pacifica?

answer_blocks.text: Publicly funded referrals go through Vancouver Coastal Health's Central Addiction Intake Team (CAIT) at 604-675-2455, option 1 for Adult CAIT. Outpatient alcohol and drug counsellors, mental health specialists, physicians, withdrawal management and EAP counsellors, unions and family members can all refer. If you live outside Vancouver Coastal Health or Fraser Health, Pacifica asks you to contact your own health authority or community supports for help with a referral.

faqs.question: How long is the wait for Pacifica?

answer_blocks.text: Pacifica says people applying for publicly funded treatment can expect a waitlist of about 8 to 12 weeks. While you wait, the Pre-Engagement Program offers weekly discussion groups, a community lunch, a facility tour and a readiness assessment. For private stays, call the intake coordinator at 604-809-3455 to ask about current wait times.

faqs.question: Who can attend Pacifica Treatment Centre?

answer_blocks.text: Pacifica serves adults aged 19 and over who come voluntarily, are medically stable and can speak and understand English. The program is gender inclusive and 2SLGBTQQI+ affirming, and pregnant women get priority admission. Medical, dental and legal appointments need to be finished before you arrive.

faqs.question: Does Pacifica treat mental health and trauma?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Pacifica calls its programs trauma-informed and concurrent-capable, so mental health and trauma concerns are worked on alongside substance use during primary treatment. The Resiliency program covers the second half of a residential stay and the first 8 weeks back in the community, and continuing care includes more mental health and trauma-focused therapy.

faqs.question: What is the PATH outpatient program?

answer_blocks.text: PATH, short for Professional Addiction Treatment at Home, is Pacifica's 16-week virtual outpatient program for adults who want to keep living at home and working. Weeks 1 to 8 include two psychoeducation sessions, two therapist-led groups and one individual session each week, and weeks 9 to 16 drop to one weekly group plus individual counselling. It costs $7,500, and bursaries of up to 50% are available based on financial need.

faqs.question: Where is Pacifica and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: Pacifica is at 1755 East 11th Avenue in East Vancouver, on a quiet residential street a short walk from SkyTrain. Downtown Vancouver is about 15 minutes by car or transit, and Burnaby is about 15 minutes. People coming from Vancouver Island can take the Swartz Bay to Tsawwassen ferry, which makes the trip from Victoria about 3.5 hours.

faqs.question: What happens after I leave Pacifica?

answer_blocks.text: Everyone who finishes primary treatment leaves with a personal continuing care plan. That includes group therapy sessions, virtual groups and one-to-one counselling, plus alumni services such as weekly on-site meetings, Thursday Alumni Night, peer mentoring and volunteering. Graduates also keep a Vancouver community centre fitness pass for 9 months after they finish.

faqs.question: Can I have visitors or use my phone at Pacifica?

answer_blocks.text: Pacifica asks for 14 days with no outside contact at the start of treatment, unless it is arranged before admission or there are special circumstances. After that you can use the house telephone at set times. Laptops, mobile phones and devices with screens are not allowed, so for current visitor rules call 604-872-5517, extension 222.
